meta.title: Download · Aethyr
meta.description: Download the Aethyr plugin for Unreal Engine 5. The Unreal modules come as source for any engine version, and the MCP server comes precompiled.

article.heading: Summon Aethyr.
article.lead: Two zips, one plugin. Both carry the MCP server already compiled. The difference is whether the Unreal modules come as source, ready to build against your engine, or prebuilt for UE 5.8.

sections.heading: Get the plugin
sections.html:
◈ Any engine versionAethyr pluginUE 5.7 · 5.8modules as sourceserver precompiled↓DownloadAethyr-plugin.zip◈ Drop-in for UE 5.8Aethyr plugin, precompiledUE 5.8no build stepserver precompiled↓DownloadAethyr-plugin-precompiled.zip

Every release lives at aethyrgames/aethyr-mcp-releases on GitHub.

sections.heading: Which zip?
sections.html:
• On UE 5.8? Take the precompiled zip. Unzip it and launch the editor, nothing to build.
  • On another engine version, or you'd rather build it yourself? Take Aethyr-plugin.zip. The Unreal modules come as C++ source and compile against your engine.

At time of writing the source zip compiles on UE 5.7 and 5.8. UE 5.6 is meant to work too. No automated check covers it yet.

sections.heading: What's in the zip
sections.html:
• Source/AethyrEditor and Source/AethyrRuntime: the two Unreal modules, as C++ source.
  • Binaries/Win64/AethyrMcp.exe: the MCP server. It doesn't link against the engine, which lets one build cover every engine version.
  • Claude/: skills and an audit agent that teach your AI assistant to use the tools well.
  • SETUP.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and README.md: setup and usage guides, written so an AI assistant can follow them.
  • NOTICE.md: third-party notices.

The precompiled zip adds the built module DLLs. Releases up to 0.1.1 leave SETUP.md and CLAUDE.md out of it.

sections.heading: Install
sections.html:
1. Unzip into your project's Plugins folder. You should end up with Plugins/Aethyr/Aethyr.uplugin.
  2. Source zip only: build the modules (next section). In a C++ project you can also open the project and let the editor rebuild them when it asks.
  3. Connect your AI client. The source zip carries Plugins/Aethyr/SETUP.md, a setup guide for AI assistants. Point yours at it and ask it to set the plugin up. With a precompiled zip that doesn't have it, follow Connect your AI.

Writes are on in this build. Every write tool works out of the box. Set AETHYR_READ_ONLY=1 in the server's environment for a session that can only read.

Engine not found? If AethyrMcp.exe doctor reports "engine directory not configured", set AETHYR_ENGINE_DIR to your engine root, like C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.8. Aethyr 0.1.1 and older only find engines registered by a source build, not Launcher installs.

Windows blocked the files? A browser download carries a downloaded-from-the-internet mark. Run Unblock-File .\Aethyr-plugin.zip before you extract it.

sections.heading: Build for your engine
sections.html:
This compiles the plugin against the engine you run it from. You'll need that engine and Visual Studio's C++ build tools.

"<Engine>\Engine\Build\BatchFiles\RunUAT.bat" BuildPlugin -Plugin="<Unzipped>\Aethyr\Aethyr.uplugin" -Package="C:\AethyrBuild" -TargetPlatforms=Win64

The package folder gets the built modules without the server exe or the docs. Copy its binaries into the plugin you unzipped:

robocopy "C:\AethyrBuild\Binaries" "<YourProject>\Plugins\Aethyr\Binaries" /E /XF *.pdb

Keep the package path short. Unreal Build Tool fails without printing a compiler error once an intermediate file path passes 260 characters. A folder like C:\AethyrBuild stays well under that.

sections.heading: Check the download
sections.html:
Every release carries a SHA256SUMS file. Hash your download in PowerShell:

Get-FileHash .\Aethyr-plugin.zip -Algorithm SHA256

The hash should match that file's line in SHA256SUMS. Case doesn't matter. Older versions are on the releases page.
